question.text: Which of the following is a type I region in two-dimensional space?
question.explanation:

where $f$ and $g$ are continuous functions.

A type I region has the property that a vertical line drawn through the region intersects the region in a single interval only.

question.explanation:
A type II region can be written as

\[ D = \big\{ (x,y) \: : \: a \leq y \leq b, \quad g(y) \leq x \leq f(y) \big\}, \]

where $f$ and $g$ are continuous functions.

To express the given region as a type II region, we first rewrite all of the given curves as functions of $y\mathbin{:}$

\[ y = 2(x-1)^3+1 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad x = \sqrt[3]{\dfrac{y-1}{2}}+1 \]

The function $x=0$ is already written as a function of $y.$

Notice that the region lies between the horizontal lines $y=1$ and $y=3.$ So, we have $1 \leq y \leq 3.$

We draw a horizontal arrow through the region to determine the left function $g(y)$ and the right function $f(y).$ A horizontal line should intersect the region in a single interval only for it to be a type II region.

The horizontal line enters the region through the lower function $x=0$ and leaves through the upper function $x=\sqrt[3]{\dfrac{y-1}{2}}+1.$ So, we have $0 \leq x \leq \sqrt[3]{\dfrac{y-1}{2}}+1.$

Therefore, we obtain \[ D= \bigg\{ (x,y) \: : \: 1 \leq y \leq 3, \: 0 \leq x \leq \sqrt[3]{\dfrac{y-1}{2}}+1 \bigg\}. \]

example.title: Classifying a Region as Type I, Type II, Both, or Neither

question.text:
Which of the following statements are true regarding the triangle bounded between the lines $y=1-x,$ $y=x-1,$ and $x=0?$

  1. It is a type I region
  2. It is a type II region
  3. It's neither a type I nor a type II region
question.explanation:
First, notice that \begin{align*} y=1-x \qquad & \Longrightarrow\qquad x=1-y \\ y=x-1 \qquad & \Longrightarrow\qquad x=y+1 . \end{align*}

Now, let's sketch our region.

We have the following:

  • Any vertical line through the region intersects it on a single interval. Furthermore, we can represent our region as \[ D = \big\{ (x,y) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \: x-1 \leq y \leq 1-x \big\}. \] So, this is a type I region.

  • Any horizontal line through the region intersects it on a single interval. Furthermore, we can represent our region as \[ D = \big\{ (x,y) \: : \: -1 \leq y \leq 1, \: 0 \leq x \leq 1-|y| \big\}. \] So, this is a type II region.

Therefore, only statements I and II are true.

example.title: Classifying a Region as Type I, Type II, Both, or Neither

question.text:
Which of the following statements are true regarding the finite region bounded between the curves $y=x^3$ and $y=\sqrt[3]{x},$ in the first quadrant?

  1. It is a type I region
  2. It is a type II region
  3. It's neither a type I nor a type II region
question.explanation:
First, notice that \begin{align*} y=x^3 \qquad & \Longrightarrow\qquad x = \sqrt[3]{y} \\ y=\sqrt[3]{x} \qquad & \Longrightarrow\qquad x=y^3 . \end{align*}

Now, let's sketch our region.

We have the following:

  • Any vertical line through the region intersects it on a single interval. Furthermore, we can represent our region as \[ D = \big\{ (x,y) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \: x^3 \leq y \leq \sqrt[3]{x} \big\}. \] So, this is a type I region.

  • Any horizontal line through the region intersects it on a single interval. Furthermore, we can represent our region as \[ D = \big\{ (x,y) \: : \: 0 \leq y \leq 1, \: y^3 \leq x \leq \sqrt[3]{y} \big\}. \] So, this is a type II region.

Therefore, only statements I and II are true.
